# Golden data – original method (Python mainFun + R, Scrucca 2014)

Reference results of the original BankFullDetection method, used to validate the
future pure numpy/scipy implementation in `bankfull_core/`.
**Do not edit or regenerate these files** unless the procedure below is deliberately re-run.

Generated on 2026-11-06.

## Environment
| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| R | 4.6.2 (`C:\Program Files\R\R-4.6.2\bin\Rscript.exe`), base packages only |
| R RNG | `Mersenne-Twister`, `Inversion`, `sample.kind = "Rejection"` (R default since 3.6.0) |
| Python | 3.12.3 (QGIS 3.34.7, `C:\Program Files\QGIS 3.34.7\apps\Python312\python.exe`) |
| numpy | 1.26.4 |
| shapely | 2.0.3 |

Note: the original plugin (2014) ran on R < 3.6, whose `sample()` used `sample.kind = "Rounding"`.
CV folds, and therefore `spar1se` and the maxima, are not expected to match historical runs exactly.

## Parameters
- `nVsteps = 100`: `depts = linspace(minY + 0.1, maxY - 0.1, 100)`; profile closed at `maxY + 1`.
- Smoothing: `smooth.spline`, 10-fold CV (balanced folds), `spar` grid `log(seq(1, e, length = 100))`, 1-SE rule.
- Seed: `set.seed(1000 + seq)` before each section, `seq` = 1-based progressive index of the section
  (files in alphabetical order, sections in order of first appearance in the file).
- Time limit per section in R: 120 s (guards the original `while(check)` loop).
- Bankfull: first R maximum with hydraulic depth `>= minVdep`, `minVdep ∈ {1.0, 0.2}`.

## Inputs
- `tests/data/sections/arno.csv`: real sections exported with `golden_tools/export_sections_qgis.py`.
- `tests/data/sections/synthetic.csv`: generated by `golden_tools/make_synthetic.py`
  (1 trapezoid, 2 inner bench, 3 two depressions, 4 smooth parabola without clear banks).

## Files
| File | Columns | Producer |
|---|---|---|
| `curves.csv` | source_file, section_id, seq, step, depth, hyd_depth (A/W), hyd_radius (A/P) | make_curves.py |
| `curves_meta.csv` | source_file, section_id, seq, n_points, minx, maxx, minY, maxY, terrace_ok, error | make_curves.py |
| `r_summary.csv` | source_file, section_id, seq, seed, status, error, sparmin, spar1se, n_iter, n_candidates, n_converged, n_maxima, out_kind | run_golden.R |
| `r_folds.csv` | source_file, section_id, point_index, fold | run_golden.R |
| `r_cv.csv` | source_file, section_id, spar, df, cv_error, se | run_golden.R |
| `r_maxima.csv` | source_file, section_id, k, x (depth), y (hyd. depth) | run_golden.R |
| `r_fitted.csv` | source_file, section_id, point_index, x, y, yhat (smoothed curve at input points) | run_golden.R |
| `bankfull.csv` | source_file, section_id, minVdep, bankfull_z, left_dist, right_dist, n_channels, error, bankfull_hyd_depth, note | make_bankfull.py |

- `point_index` and `step` are 1-based and refer to the 100 depth steps.
- `n_iter` > 1 means the original `while(check)` loop re-ran CV because no Newton–Raphson root converged.
- `terrace_ok = 0` / note `terrace_crash`: the original mainFun would have raised on `terrace[0]`
  (no raw local maximum); the bankfull is still reported because it does not depend on it.
- `out_kind = list_empty`: Newton converged only to non-maxima; the original R code then returns
  a 1x2 list matrix of `numeric(0)` instead of an empty matrix, so the Python fallback is skipped
  and the original mainFun fails (error `r_no_local_max` in `bankfull.csv`). Exported as 0 maxima.
- `bankfull.csv` error codes: `curve_error`, `r_error`, `r_no_local_max`, `no_max_ge_minvdep`
  (no maximum `>= minVdep`: IndexError in the original). Note `fallback_last_point`: R found no
  maxima and the original fallback (last curve point) was used.
- Real numbers are written with 17 significant digits.

## Known behaviours of the original method
These are reproduced on purpose: the golden data describe the original method, not a corrected one.
A future implementation may fix them, but must then document the deviation against these files.

1. **Ineffective 1-SE rule (`spar1se = sparmin`).** In `cv.smooth.spline`,
   `i <- which(cv.error[which(spar >= est)] <= oneserule)[1]` always returns 1: the first element
   of `cv.error[spar >= est]` is the CV error at `est` itself (the minimum), which is always
   `<= min + se`. Hence `est1se = est` and the fit uses the CV-minimum spar. Verified on all
   12 sections of `r_summary.csv` (`sparmin == spar1se`). The intended 1-SE rule would pick the
   largest (smoothest) spar with `cv.error <= oneserule`.
2. **Trapezoid without bankfull (synthetic 1).** The A/W curve has a clear maximum at z ≈ 2.98,
   but Newton–Raphson, started from the 2 sign-change candidates of f', converges only to roots
   with f'' >= 0. `local.max` is empty and R returns a 1x2 list matrix of `numeric(0)`
   (`out_kind = list_empty`), so the Python fallback is skipped and the original mainFun fails:
   `error = r_no_local_max` for both minVdep values.
3. **Crash on `terrace[0]` (synthetic 4, parabola).** The raw A/W curve is monotonic, so
   `local_maxmin` finds no maxima and `max(maxima_ranks)` / `terrace[0]` raise in the original
   mainFun, even though the bankfull itself does not depend on it (`terrace_ok = 0`,
   note `terrace_crash`). On the same section R finds no stationary point and the fallback puts
   the bankfull at the last curve point, z = maxY − 0.1 = 3.9 (note `fallback_last_point`).
4. **Bankfull too low with two depressions and minVdep = 0.2 (synthetic 3).** The bankfull is the
   *first* R maximum (lowest depth) with A/W >= minVdep. With 0.2 this is the in-channel maximum
   at z ≈ 0.447 (A/W ≈ 0.41) inside the deeper depression only: 1 channel, banks 35.1–42.7,
   instead of the level ≈ 1.94 below the bar (2 channels) found with minVdep = 1.0 or the
   bank top at z ≈ 3. The result is very sensitive to minVdep.
